design_issues.screen: PublicShell header (when a logged-in user visits /kapcsolat, /aszf, etc.)
issues: Top-right link still says 'Belépés' and points to /belepes even though the user is authenticated. Minor UX: could read 'Vissza az alkalmazásba' → '/' for logged-in users. Non-blocking.

action_items: OPTIONAL: PublicShell.jsx – show 'Vissza az alkalmazásba' (link to '/') instead of 'Belépés' when user is authenticated, to avoid confusion when a logged-in user opens a public link like /kapcsolat.

OPTIONAL (from iter3, still open): Jobs.jsx EMPTY.status='uj' and Quotes.jsx EMPTY.status='vazlat' remain — browser masks it via select fallback, but should read 'erdeklodo' / 'piszkozat' for clarity.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 1057 lines. Still readable but consider splitting into auth.py / crud.py / pdf.py / email.py / search.py before further growth.
/api/search performs 6 sequential Mongo queries per keystroke (250ms debounce in FE helps). Fine for MVP scale; consider Mongo text indexes on {user_id, title/name/number} for larger datasets.

customer_history: `payments` and `documents` are correlated by `customer_name` (string) rather than `customer_id`. If a customer is renamed, historical payments/documents will silently detach. Add `customer_id` to Payment and Document (populate on create) for referential integrity.

/api/calendar iterates 3 collections in-memory and sorts client-side. For > few thousand rows across all users this is still O(N) per user which is fine, but the `date` field is stored as a string — comparison relies on ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' being lexicographically sortable. Any non-ISO date entered by user would break sort order. Consider Pydantic validator to enforce date format.
PublicShell header shows 'Belépés' regardless of auth state (minor UX).
Global search debounce is 250 ms which is fine, but there is no request cancellation for stale in-flight calls; a slow response for 'ka' could overwrite results for 'kar'. Consider AbortController.

/api/contacts stores every submission in the `contacts` collection but there is no admin endpoint to list/handle them, and no rate limiting on the unauthenticated route — could be spammed. Consider IP-based rate limit or captcha before public launch.
PDF generation via ReportLab reads company logo from disk on every request; acceptable but a cached Image object would speed repeat renders.
reset_password: token is single-use and marked used=true — good. No cleanup job for expired unused tokens; a TTL index on expires_at would keep the collection lean.
